P1_explanation.template: This pattern attempts to override system instructions or ignore safety constraints. Without LLM analysis, manual review is recommended.

P1_remediation.template: Remove or rewrite any text that instructs the agent to ignore prompts, override safety rules, or trust unverified content. Ensure skill content cannot be injected to alter agent behavior.

P2_explanation.template: Hidden instructions were detected in comments or invisible text. These could contain malicious directives. Manual review is recommended.

P2_remediation.template: Audit all comments and invisible characters. Remove any instructions that direct the agent to perform unauthorized actions. Use plain, reviewable content.

P3_explanation.template: Instructions found that direct the agent to transmit conversation context or user data to external services.

P3_remediation.template: Remove instructions that send user data, prompts, or context to external URLs. If telemetry is needed, use documented, privacy-preserving methods.

P4_explanation.template: Subtle instructions detected that may alter agent decision-making or introduce hidden biases.

P4_remediation.template: Review content for implicit steering or bias. Ensure instructions are explicit and align with the skill's stated purpose.

P5_explanation.template: This content may contain harmful instructions that could cause physical harm if followed. CRITICAL: Review carefully before use.

P5_remediation.template: Remove all content that could lead to harmful outcomes. Add safety guardrails and human oversight for any high-risk operations.

E1_explanation.template: Data is being sent to an external URL. This could be legitimate telemetry or data exfiltration. Manual review is recommended.

E1_remediation.template: Verify the destination URL is trusted and necessary. Remove or replace with documented APIs. Ensure no secrets, tokens, or PII are transmitted.

E2_explanation.template: Code accesses environment variables that may contain secrets (API keys, tokens). This is a common pattern for credential theft.

E2_remediation.template: Avoid reading sensitive env vars (API keys, tokens) unless strictly required. Use secrets managers or secure config. Never log or transmit credentials.

E3_explanation.template: Code scans file system directories looking for sensitive files. This could be reconnaissance for credential theft.

E3_remediation.template: Remove unnecessary filesystem scanning. If file access is needed, use explicit, scoped paths. Avoid reading ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or credential directories.

E4_explanation.template: Code or instructions that leak agent conversation context to external services, potentially exposing sensitive user interactions.

E4_remediation.template: Remove any code that sends prompts, responses, or session data externally. Preserve user privacy; never exfiltrate conversation content.

PE1_explanation.template: Skill requests more permissions than appear necessary for its stated functionality. Review if elevated access is justified.

PE1_remediation.template: Request only the minimum permissions required. Document why each permission is needed. Remove broad permissions like '*' or 'all'.

PE2_explanation.template: Commands invoke sudo or root privileges. Verify this elevated access is necessary and justified.

PE2_remediation.template: Avoid sudo/root unless strictly required. Prefer least-privilege patterns. If elevation is needed, document the justification and scope.

PE3_explanation.template: Code accesses credential files (SSH keys, AWS credentials, etc.). This could indicate credential theft attempts.

PE3_remediation.template: Remove references to credential paths. Use environment variables or secrets managers. For docs, use placeholder paths (e.g., /path/to/config). Never load .env or token files in production code paths.

SC1_explanation.template: Dependencies lack version pinning, allowing potential malicious package updates. Consider pinning versions.

SC1_remediation.template: Pin all dependency versions in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml. Use exact versions (==) or compatible ranges. Run pip-audit regularly.

SC2_explanation.template: Remote code is downloaded and executed. This bypasses code review and could introduce malicious code.

SC2_remediation.template: Avoid downloading and executing remote scripts. Use trusted packages from PyPI/npm. If remote fetch is required, verify checksums and use HTTPS.

SC3_explanation.template: Code contains obfuscation (base64, hex encoding with execution). This is often used to hide malicious functionality.

SC3_remediation.template: Remove obfuscated code. Use plain, readable implementations. Obfuscation hinders security review and raises trust concerns.

EA1_explanation.template: Skill grants unrestricted tool access without appropriate constraints. An agent with unfettered tool access can perform arbitrary actions including file modification, network requests, and code execution.

EA1_remediation.template: Restrict tool access to only the tools required for the skill's stated purpose. Use an explicit allowlist rather than granting blanket access.

EA2_explanation.template: Skill enables autonomous high-impact decisions without human-in-the-loop verification. Critical operations (destructive commands, financial transactions, data deletion) should require explicit user confirmation.

EA2_remediation.template: Add human-in-the-loop confirmation for destructive, irreversible, or high-impact operations. Never auto-execute commands that modify files, send data, or alter system state.

EA3_explanation.template: Skill's behavior or capabilities extend beyond its stated purpose. Scope creep allows an agent to perform actions unrelated to its documented functionality, increasing the attack surface.

EA3_remediation.template: Limit the skill's scope to its documented purpose. Remove instructions that enable the agent to perform actions outside its stated functionality.

EA4_explanation.template: Skill allows unbounded resource consumption (API calls, storage, compute). Without rate limits or quotas, a compromised or misbehaving agent can cause denial-of-service or cost overruns.

EA4_remediation.template: Set explicit rate limits, timeouts, and resource quotas for API calls, file operations, and compute. Implement circuit breakers for runaway loops.

OH1_explanation.template: Model output is used without validation or sanitization. Unvalidated output injected into downstream contexts (SQL, shell, HTML) enables injection attacks and arbitrary code execution.

OH1_remediation.template: Validate and sanitize all model output before using it in downstream contexts. Use parameterized queries for SQL, shell quoting for commands, and HTML encoding for web output.

OH2_explanation.template: Output from one security context is used in another without boundary enforcement. Cross-context output flow can leak sensitive information or escalate privileges across trust boundaries.

OH2_remediation.template: Enforce strict context boundaries. Do not pass output from one security domain into another without explicit validation and redaction of sensitive content.

OH3_explanation.template: Output size or generation rate is not bounded. Unbounded output enables denial-of-service through resource exhaustion, log flooding, or context-window stuffing.

OH3_remediation.template: Set explicit limits on output length, generation count, and rate. Use max_tokens and truncation to prevent unbounded output.

P6_explanation.template: Skill contains instructions that could directly expose system prompts, internal rules, or hidden instructions to users or external parties.

P6_remediation.template: Remove any instructions that reveal, print, or output system prompts or internal rules. System instructions should never be exposed to end users.

P7_explanation.template: Skill contains patterns that could indirectly extract system prompts through rephrasing, translation, summarization, or side-channel techniques.

P7_remediation.template: Guard against indirect extraction by refusing to summarize, translate, or rephrase system instructions. Add explicit anti-extraction clauses.

P8_explanation.template: Skill contains patterns that exfiltrate system prompts or internal instructions via tool calls (file writes, network requests, logging).

P8_remediation.template: Prevent system prompts from being written to files, sent via network, or logged. Treat system instructions as confidential and filter them from all tool outputs.

MP1_explanation.template: Skill injects content designed to persist in agent memory or context across interactions. Persistent injection can alter agent behavior long after the initial interaction.

MP1_remediation.template: Do not allow untrusted input to persist in agent memory or context. Validate all content before storing and implement memory isolation between sessions.

MP2_explanation.template: Skill attempts to fill the context window with filler content, displacing legitimate instructions and safety constraints. This can degrade agent performance or bypass safety boundaries.

MP2_remediation.template: Implement context-window management that detects and rejects padding or stuffing attempts. Prioritize system instructions over user-injected content.

MP3_explanation.template: Skill manipulates agent memory, state, or stored context. Memory corruption can alter personality, override safety rules, or cause unpredictable behavior.

MP3_remediation.template: Protect agent memory and state from modification by untrusted content. Use read-only memory for critical instructions and validate all state changes.

TM1_explanation.template: Tool parameters are crafted to achieve unintended or unsafe behavior. Parameter abuse can bypass intended safety checks (e.g. shell=True, --force, dangerous glob patterns).

TM1_remediation.template: Validate all tool parameters against an allowlist. Reject dangerous parameter values (shell=True, --force, -rf /) and use safe defaults.

TM2_explanation.template: Tool calls are chained to bypass individual safety checks or escalate capabilities beyond what any single tool call would allow.

TM2_remediation.template: Limit tool chaining depth and validate the output of each tool before passing it to the next. Require explicit user approval for multi-step chains.

TM3_explanation.template: Tool defaults are unsafe or overly permissive (e.g. disabled TLS verification, no authentication, world-writable permissions). Unsafe defaults widen the attack surface.

TM3_remediation.template: Override unsafe defaults with secure settings (verify=True, auth required, restrictive permissions). Review and harden all tool configurations.

RA1_explanation.template: Skill modifies its own code, configuration, or behavior at runtime. Self-modification enables an agent to escalate privileges, disable safety constraints, or install persistent backdoors.

RA1_remediation.template: Prevent the skill from modifying its own code, SKILL.md, or configuration files. Treat skill files as read-only at runtime.

RA2_explanation.template: Skill establishes unauthorized persistence across sessions via cron jobs, startup scripts, or state files. Session persistence allows an attacker to maintain access beyond the current interaction.

RA2_remediation.template: Remove any persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, startup scripts, state files). Skills should not maintain state across sessions without explicit user consent.

SC4_explanation.template: Dependency has known vulnerabilities (CVEs). Using packages with unpatched security flaws exposes the environment to known exploits.

SC4_remediation.template: Update the dependency to a patched version that addresses the known CVE. Check OSV (osv.dev) or NVD for details on the vulnerability.

SC5_explanation.template: Dependency appears abandoned or unmaintained. Abandoned packages no longer receive security patches, leaving known and future vulnerabilities unaddressed.

SC5_remediation.template: Replace the abandoned dependency with an actively maintained alternative. Check the package's repository for last commit date and open issues.

SC6_explanation.template: Package name closely resembles a popular package, suggesting possible typosquatting. Attackers publish malicious packages with similar names to trick developers into installing them.

SC6_remediation.template: Verify the package name is correct and not a typosquatting variant. Compare against the official package name on PyPI or npm.

TR1_explanation.template: Skill uses overly broad trigger patterns that match common words or phrases, causing it to activate in unintended contexts and potentially shadow other skills.

TR1_remediation.template: Use specific, narrow trigger patterns that match only the skill's intended use case. Avoid single-word or common-phrase triggers.

TR2_explanation.template: Skill trigger shadows a common built-in command or another skill's trigger, potentially intercepting requests meant for trusted functionality.

TR2_remediation.template: Choose triggers that do not conflict with built-in commands or other skills. Prefix with a unique namespace if necessary.

TR3_explanation.template: Skill trigger uses vague or generic keywords designed to maximize activation frequency rather than target specific use cases.

TR3_remediation.template: Use descriptive triggers that clearly indicate the skill's purpose rather than generic keywords designed to maximize activation.

TT1_explanation.template: Data flows directly from a source (env vars, files, network) to a sink (network output, exec, file write) without intermediate validation.

TT1_remediation.template: Add validation or sanitization between the data source and sink. Never pass raw source data directly to a sink without checking its content.

TT2_explanation.template: Data from a source is assigned to a variable that is later passed to a sink, creating a variable-mediated taint flow.

TT2_remediation.template: Validate tainted variables before passing them to sinks. Use allowlists, type checks, or sanitization functions on data from external sources.

TT3_explanation.template: Credentials or environment variables flow to a network sink. This is a high-confidence indicator of credential exfiltration.

TT3_remediation.template: Never send credentials or environment variables over the network. Use secure credential stores and avoid transmitting secrets in request bodies or URLs.

TT4_explanation.template: File contents flow to a network sink. This may indicate data exfiltration of sensitive files.

TT4_remediation.template: Validate and filter file contents before sending over the network. Ensure sensitive files (credentials, configs) are never transmitted to external endpoints.

TT5_explanation.template: External input (network, user) flows to a code execution sink. This enables remote code execution or command injection.

TT5_remediation.template: Never pass external input to exec(), eval(), os.system(), or subprocess without strict validation. Use allowlists and parameterized commands instead.

AST1_explanation.template: Direct exec() call allows arbitrary code execution. An attacker can inject code that runs with the full privileges of the process.

AST1_remediation.template: Replace exec() with a safe alternative. If dynamic execution is required, use a sandboxed environment or restricted eval with __builtins__ disabled.

AST2_explanation.template: Direct eval() call evaluates arbitrary expressions. This can be exploited to execute malicious code or exfiltrate data.

AST2_remediation.template: Replace eval() with ast.literal_eval() for data parsing, or use explicit parsing logic. Never evaluate untrusted strings.

AST3_explanation.template: Dynamic __import__() can load arbitrary modules at runtime, bypassing static analysis and potentially importing malicious code.

AST3_remediation.template: Use standard import statements instead of __import__(). If dynamic loading is needed, use importlib with an allowlist of permitted modules.

AST4_explanation.template: subprocess module calls execute external commands. Without careful input validation, this enables command injection.

AST4_remediation.template: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and an explicit argument list. Validate all inputs and avoid passing user-controlled data to commands.

AST5_explanation.template: os.system() and os exec-family calls run shell commands with the process's full privileges, enabling arbitrary command execution.

AST5_remediation.template: Replace os.system() with subprocess.run(shell=False). Use explicit argument lists and validate all command inputs.

AST6_explanation.template: compile() creates code objects from strings. When combined with exec()/eval(), it enables obfuscated code execution.

AST6_remediation.template: Avoid compile() with dynamic strings. If code generation is needed, use templates or AST manipulation with strict validation.

AST7_explanation.template: Dynamic getattr() with a non-literal attribute name can access arbitrary object attributes, potentially bypassing access controls.

AST7_remediation.template: Replace dynamic getattr() with explicit attribute access or a dictionary lookup with an allowlist of permitted attributes.

AST8_explanation.template: A dangerous execution chain combines code execution (exec/eval) with a dynamic source (network, encoded data, dynamic import), creating a high-confidence attack vector.

AST8_remediation.template: Remove the execution chain entirely. Never pass network data, decoded bytes, or dynamically imported code to exec()/eval(). Use structured data formats instead.

YR1_explanation.template: YARA rule matched a known malware signature (reverse shell, backdoor, ransomware, C2 framework, or info stealer).

YR1_remediation.template: Remove the malware payload or compromised file entirely. Investigate how it entered the skill and audit all other artifacts for additional indicators of compromise.

YR2_explanation.template: YARA rule matched a known webshell pattern (PHP, Python, JSP, or ASPX webshell).

YR2_remediation.template: Remove the webshell code immediately. Webshells provide unauthorized remote command execution. Audit the skill for additional backdoors or persistence mechanisms.

YR3_explanation.template: YARA rule matched cryptocurrency mining indicators (stratum protocol, mining pools, miner binaries, or cryptojacking scripts).

YR3_remediation.template: Remove all cryptocurrency mining code, pool references, and miner binaries. Mining in agent skills is unauthorized resource abuse. Report the skill as malicious.

YR4_explanation.template: YARA rule matched a hack tool or exploit indicator (offensive tools, reconnaissance, privilege escalation, or exploit frameworks).

YR4_remediation.template: Remove offensive tool references and exploit code. Legitimate agent skills should not contain penetration testing tools, exploit frameworks, or reconnaissance utilities.

LP1_explanation.template: Code uses capabilities (network, shell, file write, etc.) not covered by declared permissions. The skill does more than it claims, which may indicate deceptive intent.

LP1_remediation.template: Add the missing permission to SKILL.md, or remove the code that requires it.

LP2_explanation.template: Permission list contains a wildcard ('*' or 'all'), granting blanket access with no least-privilege boundary. This disables permission-based security controls entirely.

LP2_remediation.template: Replace wildcard permissions ('*', 'all', 'full', 'any') with an explicit list of required permissions.

LP3_explanation.template: Skill has no permissions field in its manifest but code uses detectable capabilities. Without declared permissions, the skill's intent is opaque and cannot be validated.

LP3_remediation.template: Add a 'permissions' field to SKILL.md listing the capabilities this skill requires.

LP4_explanation.template: Permission is declared but no corresponding code capability was detected. This may indicate removed functionality or pre-staging for future abuse.

LP4_remediation.template: Remove the declared permission if the corresponding capability is no longer used.

TP1_explanation.template: Hidden instructions detected in skill metadata (description, triggers, or parameters). These concealed directives can steer LLM behavior without the user's knowledge.

TP1_remediation.template: Remove hidden content (HTML comments, markdown comments, zero-width characters, base64 blobs) from metadata fields. Metadata should contain plain, visible text only.

TP2_explanation.template: Unicode deception detected in skill identifiers or descriptions. Homoglyphs, RTL overrides, or invisible characters can make malicious content appear benign.

TP2_remediation.template: Replace non-ASCII characters in identifiers with ASCII equivalents. Remove RTL override and invisible formatting characters.

TP3_explanation.template: Instruction injection patterns found in parameter descriptions or default values. Parameter metadata is read by LLMs and can override intended behavior.

TP3_remediation.template: Remove injection patterns, system tokens, and suspicious content from parameter descriptions and default values.

TP4_explanation.template: Skill description does not match actual code behavior. The declared purpose diverges from what the code actually does, indicating possible deception.

TP4_remediation.template: Update the skill description to accurately reflect all capabilities, or remove undeclared functionality.

TP1_data_uri_message.template: Data URI found in '{p0}': potential hidden payload delivery.

TP1_data_uri_explanation.template: Data URIs embedded in metadata fields can encode and deliver hidden payloads to AI agents processing the manifest.

TP1_data_uri_remediation.template: Remove data URIs from metadata fields. Metadata should contain plain text only.

TP1_html_comment_message.template: HTML comment found in '{p0}': potential hidden instruction.

TP1_html_comment_explanation.template: HTML comments in tool metadata are invisible to users but may be processed by AI agents, enabling hidden instruction injection.

TP1_html_comment_remediation.template: Remove HTML comments from metadata fields. Metadata should contain plain, visible text only.

TP1_markdown_comment_message.template: Markdown comment found in '{p0}': potential hidden instruction.

TP1_markdown_comment_explanation.template: Markdown-style comments in metadata fields may hide instructions from users while still being processed by AI systems.

TP1_markdown_comment_remediation.template: Remove markdown comments from metadata fields.

TP1_zero_width_message.template: Zero-width character(s) followed by visible text found in '{p0}': potential steganographic instruction.

TP1_zero_width_explanation.template: Zero-width Unicode characters are invisible to humans but detectable by AI. When followed by visible text, they indicate hidden content injection.

TP1_zero_width_remediation.template: Strip zero-width Unicode characters (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D) from all metadata fields.

TP1_base64_message.template: Base64-encoded blob found in '{p0}': potential hidden encoded instruction.

TP1_base64_explanation.template: Long base64-encoded strings in metadata fields may encode hidden instructions intended to be decoded and executed by AI agents.

TP1_base64_remediation.template: Remove base64-encoded blobs from metadata fields. Metadata should contain only human-readable plain text.

TP2_direction_message.template: RTL/directional override character(s) found in '{p0}': {p1}. Text direction manipulation detected.

TP2_direction_explanation.template: RTL override characters (U+202E, U+202D, U+2066-U+2069) can reverse text rendering to make malicious content appear benign.

TP2_direction_remediation.template: Remove all directional override Unicode characters from metadata fields.

TP4_mismatch_message.template: Description-behavior mismatch: declared purpose is '{p0}' but code also performs: {p1}.

TP4_mismatch_remediation.template: Update the skill description to accurately reflect all capabilities, or remove undeclared functionality from the implementation.

TP2_homoglyph_message.template: Homoglyph characters detected in identifier '{p0}': {p1}. Visual spoofing of identifier name.

TP2_homoglyph_explanation.template: Confusable Unicode characters (e.g., Cyrillic or Greek lookalikes of Latin letters) can make a malicious tool name appear identical to a trusted one.

TP2_homoglyph_remediation.template: Replace all non-ASCII characters in identifier fields with their ASCII equivalents. Use a Unicode normalization/confusables check in CI.

TP2_invisible_message.template: Invisible formatting character(s) found in identifier '{p0}': {p1}.

TP2_invisible_explanation.template: Invisible Unicode formatting characters (soft hyphen U+00AD, CGJ U+034F, word joiner U+2060) inserted into identifiers create visually identical but technically different names.

TP2_invisible_remediation.template: Strip invisible formatting characters (U+00AD, U+034F, U+2060) from all identifier fields.

TP2_mixed_script_message.template: Mixed script detected in identifier '{p0}': {p1}. Multiple Unicode scripts in a single identifier name.

TP2_mixed_script_explanation.template: Mixing characters from multiple Unicode scripts in a single identifier is a common technique to create visually ambiguous tool names.

TP2_mixed_script_remediation.template: Restrict identifier fields to a single Unicode script. Prefer ASCII-only identifiers.

TP3_override_message.template: Instruction override phrase in parameter '{p0}' description: '{p1}'.

TP3_override_explanation.template: Instruction-override phrases in parameter descriptions can hijack AI agent behavior when the tool description is processed as a prompt.

TP3_override_remediation.template: Remove instruction-override language from parameter descriptions. Descriptions should explain the parameter's purpose only.

TP3_system_token_message.template: System prompt token in parameter '{p0}' description: '{p1}'.

TP3_system_token_explanation.template: System prompt tokens injected into parameter descriptions may alter the AI agent's system context when the tool schema is processed.

TP3_system_token_remediation.template: Remove system prompt tokens (SYSTEM:, <system>, [INST], etc.) from parameter descriptions.

TP3_exfiltration_message.template: Potential exfiltration instruction in parameter '{p0}' description: '{p1}'.

TP3_exfiltration_explanation.template: Exfiltration-related phrases in parameter descriptions may instruct AI agents to leak conversation data or sensitive information.

TP3_exfiltration_remediation.template: Remove data transmission instructions from parameter descriptions.

TP3_length_message.template: Excessive parameter description length for '{p0}': {p1} chars (limit: {p2}).

TP3_length_explanation.template: Unusually long parameter descriptions may contain hidden instructions padded with benign content to evade simple keyword detection.

TP3_length_remediation.template: Keep parameter descriptions under {p0} characters. Move extended documentation to separate files.

TP3_default_value_message.template: Suspicious default value for parameter '{p0}': contains '{p1}'.

TP3_default_value_explanation.template: Default parameter values containing URLs or shell commands may trigger unintended network requests or command execution when used by an AI agent without explicit user input.

TP3_default_value_remediation.template: Remove URLs and shell commands from parameter default values. Default values should be safe, static, representative examples.

LP2_wildcard_message.template: Permission list contains a wildcard entry ('*', 'all', 'full', or 'any'), granting blanket access with no least-privilege boundary.

LP2_wildcard_explanation.template: Wildcard permissions disable permission-based security controls entirely. Specify only the permissions the skill actually requires.

LP2_wildcard_remediation.template: Replace '*'/'all'/'full'/'any' with an explicit list of required permissions. Request only the minimum access needed.

LP3_missing_message.template: Skill has no declared permissions but code capabilities were detected: {p0}.

LP3_missing_explanation.template: Without declared permissions the skill's intent is opaque and cannot be validated.

LP3_missing_remediation.template: Add a 'permissions' field to SKILL.md listing the capabilities this skill requires.

LP1_underdeclared_message.template: Code capability '{p0}' detected in {p1} but not covered by declared permissions.

LP1_underdeclared_explanation.template: The skill uses '{p0}' capability that is not listed in its permissions. This may indicate deceptive intent or missing permission declarations.

LP1_underdeclared_remediation.template: Add the '{p0}' permission to SKILL.md, or remove the code that requires it.

LP4_overdeclared_message.template: Permission '{p0}' is declared but no corresponding code capability ({p1}) was detected.

LP4_overdeclared_explanation.template: Declared permissions with no matching code capability may indicate removed functionality or pre-staging for future abuse.

LP4_overdeclared_remediation.template: Remove the '{p0}' permission if the corresponding capability is no longer used.

SC5_abandoned.template: Abandoned Dependency: {p0} is unmaintained and no longer receives security updates

TR1_common.template: Overly Broad Trigger: '{p0}' is a common word that will activate in many unintended contexts

TR1_short.template: Overly Broad Trigger: '{p0}' is too short and may match unintended inputs

TR3_bait.template: Keyword Baiting Trigger: '{p0}' is designed to match all or most user inputs
